# New flag is more noticeable (AH-0MVCFH6I4000AWRI)

## Problem statement

On the hold-full ("HULL FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP") reward overlay the `★ New`
marker for an item the player does not yet own is rendered as a small (14 px),
muted-orange detail line **beneath** the option's description, where it reads as
just another piece of detail copy. With three options on screen, a reduced-volume
ghost fire running and a 3-2-1 countdown competing for attention, players miss the
marker and read a brand-new item as an upgrade to something they already own.

## Users

- **Player (at-a-glance scan):** "As a player whose hold has just filled, I want
  brand-new offers to jump out of the list immediately, so I can tell 'this is
  something I don't own yet' from 'this is an upgrade' without reading every
  line."
- **Player (reward readability):** "As a player I want the New marker attached to
  the item's title so I cannot lose it in the description/countdown noise."
- **Designer / tuner:** "As a designer I want the emphasis produced by a single
  shared overlay implementation, so the game and every gym show the same
  presentation and the tuning lives in one place."

## Current behaviour (existing state)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` renders each option as a three-line block:
  1. title line `${index + 1}.  ${option.name}` — 20 px, cyan `#00ffff`,
     centred at `GAME_WIDTH / 2`, with `#111111` background padding;
  2. description line (13 px, `#cccccc`) at `y + 28`;
  3. detail line (14 px) at `y + 48` — the change summary
     (e.g. `+1 Projectiles`) or the string `★ New` in orange `#ff8800`
     (`CHOICE_NEW_COLOR`). `New` takes display priority over a change summary.
- The badge is static: no weight, no motion, no glow. Its container
  `getDetailLines()` is what the scene tests assert against.
- Existing agreed behaviour: **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC4** specifies the badge as
  "a second, smaller detail line beneath the option name" and the three-line
  block is documented in the Game Design Document §4.5 and the README module
  entry for the overlay. Those two statements are what this item deliberately
  revises.
- Existing tests that pin the current presentation:
  `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` —
  `renders a "New" badge for options marked isNew` (asserts
  `getDetailLines()[0] === '★ New'`), `"New" badge takes display priority over
  changeSummary`, and `AC2 — shows a New option's description above its ★ New
  badge`.

## Desired change

1. Move the `★ New` marker to the **start of the title line**, ahead of the
   numbered name, so it is visually part of the item's heading.
2. Make it **bolder**: bold weight, larger than the current 14 px detail text,
   high-contrast treatment (stroke and/or text shadow) so it reads from a
   distance.
3. Give it **motion and light**: a continuous pulse (scale/alpha) plus a visible
   glow that intensifies with the pulse.
4. Stop repeating the marker on the detail line — the detail line keeps only the
   change summary (see Q2 below; the draft assumes removal).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Badge leads the title line.** For every option with `isNew`, the
  presetation renders the `★ New` marker on the **same row as the option title
  and to the left of that title** (reading order `★ New` → `1.` → item name), on
  the title line's vertical centre. Options without `isNew` render no marker.
- **AC2 — Bolder than before.** The marker is rendered in a bold weight with a
  font size strictly larger than the previous 14 px detail text, plus a visible
  stroke or text shadow, at a contrast that is at least as strong as the current
  `#ff8800` orange against the `#000000` backdrop.
- **AC3 — Pulses.** The marker animates continuously while the overlay is open
  with a yoyo tween over bounded properties (scale and/or alpha), period within
  600–1200 ms, scale amplitude ≤ 1.15 and alpha floor ≥ 0.6, so it stays inside
  its row (row pitch is 84 px) and never touches the title text or the
  neighbouring rows.
- **AC4 — Glows.** A visible glow accompanies the pulse (text shadow with blur
  and/or stroke) whose intensity is animated in step with AC3, remaining legible
  at every phase of the pulse.
- **AC5 — No duplicate marker, no layout regression.** The detail line no longer
  contains `★ New` (producer Q2 = A, revising AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC4); change
  summaries continue to render beneath the description;
  `getOptionLabels()` still contains the option number and name; the existing
  three-line block (title → description → detail) and row pitch are preserved.
- **AC6 — Clean teardown.** Every pulse/glow tween is stopped and the marker
  objects destroyed when the selection countdown starts
  (`AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ` teardown path) and when the scene shuts down — no
  orphaned tweens or tweens targeting destroyed text.
- **AC7 — Gym↔game parity.** The change lives once in the shared overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`), so `PlayScene` and every gym that opens it present the
  identical marker; no divergent copy is introduced.
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** Scene tests cover: marker present at the title
  line start for `isNew` options and absent otherwise; bold/larger style
  asserted; pulse tween exists with the expected target properties and is
  removed on teardown; detail line no longer carries `★ New` while change
  summaries still render. Each test asserts a behaviour, not internal constants.
- **AC9 — Documentation.** Game Design Document §4.5 and the README
  `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` entry describe the title-line marker with
  its pulse/glow, and the code comments in the scene are updated. (CHANGELOG is
  handled by the release pipeline and is out of scope.)
- **AC10 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Single shared implementation.** `MineralChoiceScene` is consumed by
  `PlayScene` and every gym (`GymFormationScene`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, …); the
  marker is implemented once there. No per-launcher option or flag.
- **Phaser 4 text only.** No new sprites or binary assets; the glow is achieved
  with Phaser text styling (`stroke`, `shadow`) and tweens.
- **Demo/attract mode safe.** The demo launcher auto-selects after a delay
  (`autoSelectMs`). The pulse must not delay, block or interfere with selection,
  the 3-2-1 countdown, or the ghost-fire metronome.
- **No new settings surface.** There is no reduced-motion setting in
  `configStore` today; this item does not add one (bounded amplitude keeps the
  motion mild). If the producer wants a visibility/reduce-motion toggle, that is
  a separate item.
- **Headless eval unaffected.** The perception-free eval arena never opens the
  overlay, so no eval-parity work is required; the existing parity tests keep
  guarding shared behaviour.

## Existing state / Desired change summary

| Aspect | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| Position | detail line under the description (`y + 48`) | start of the title line, left of `1.  <name>` |
| Weight | regular 14 px | bold, larger than 14 px, stroked/shadowed |
| Motion | none | continuous bounded pulse + glow |
| Detail line | `★ New` or change summary | change summary only |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — add the title-line marker text object,
  style constants (size/colour/stroke/shadow), pulse/glow tween creation and
  teardown, plus a test accessor (e.g. `getNewBadges()` returning the marker
  texts/tweens) alongside the existing `getOptionLabels()` / `getDetailLines()`
  accessors.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — revise the three existing
  `New` badge assertions to the new contract and add placement, style, tween and
  teardown coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 hold-full choice overlay bullet: marker
  presentation (title-line start, bold, pulsing, glowing).
- `README.md` — `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` module entry: same
  description in the three-line block summary.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** (completed) — introduced the change summary and the
  `★ New` badge as a detail line; AC4 is the statement this item revises.
- **AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD** (completed) — added the description line and the
  three-line block that positions the marker today.
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** (completed) — created the shared hold-full overlay and
  its zero-launcher-knowledge contract.
- **AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ** (completed) — countdown + teardown path the pulse must
  respect.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** (completed) — power-up levelling, which made the badge
  apply to power-ups as well as weapons (so up to three markers can be on screen
  at once).
- **AH-0MVCFB00Y004AQ2Z** (completed) — sibling hold-full-screen item, same area
  of the overlay (recent precedent for intake → implement on this screen).

## Assumptions (A1–A2 confirmed by the producer; A3–A5 are implementation defaults)

- **A1.** The marker text stays `★ New` (uppercase-initial, star prefix) rather
  than becoming `NEW` / `NEW!`; only its weight, size, position, motion and glow
  change. Rationale: it keeps the wording players have seen and keeps the
  existing string assertions meaningful.
- **A2.** The base colour stays the orange `CHOICE_NEW_COLOR` (`#ff8800`); the
  glow adds light (white/amber shadow) rather than changing the hue.
- **A3.** The pulse runs continuously for as long as the overlay is open (one
  tween per marker), rather than pulsing a fixed number of times.
- **A4.** Marker motion is implemented per-marker with the same tween
  configuration; no per-index phase offset (three markers pulsing in step is
  acceptable).
- **A5.** The marker does not change the overlay's width, centring rules or the
  row pitch; the title line is laid out as `[marker][gap][numbered name]` with
  both anchored relative to the existing centred title.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> Recorded via `/skill:intake`. All three interview questions were answered by
> the producer (2026-10-25, interactive reply), each with the recommended option
> **A**; no open questions remain.

- **Q1 — Does the marker become a separate object beside the title, or become
  part of the title string?**
  Options: **(A)** a separate text object anchored to the left of the existing
  title text, leaving `getOptionLabels()` unchanged; **(B)** prefix the title
  string (`★ New  1.  Spread Shot`).
  **Recommended:** A — keeps the tested label contract and centring intact and
  gives the marker its own tween target.
  Answer (producer, 2026-10-25, interactive reply): **A** — a separate marker
  object; `getOptionLabels()` stays unchanged.

- **Q2 — Should the `★ New` marker remain on the detail line as well?**
  Options: **(A)** remove it from the detail line (marker now lives on the title
  line; upgrades keep their summary line); **(B)** keep both (duplicate marker,
  maximum visibility but redundant); **(C)** keep the detail line unchanged and
  simply add the emphasised marker to the title as well.
  **Recommended:** A — a single marker is clearer, and duplicating `★ New` in two
  places would fight the countdown for attention.
  Answer (producer, 2026-10-25, interactive reply): **A** — remove the marker
  from the detail line; this supersedes AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC4 ("second,
  smaller detail line") and the three-line-block wording in GDD §4.5 and the
  README module entry.

- **Q3 — How strong should the motion be, and does it need an accessibility
  opt-out?**
  Options: **(A)** continuous subtle pulse (alpha 0.75↔1.0, scale 1.0↔1.08,
  ~700 ms yoyo) with a matching glow, always on; **(B)** pulse three times on
  open, then settle into a static glow; **(C)** continuous pulse plus a new
  reduce-motion/visibility toggle in settings.
  **Recommended:** A — clearly noticeable while staying inside the 84 px row and
  adding no new settings surface; C would be a separate item.
  Answer (producer, 2026-10-25, interactive reply): **A** — continuous subtle
  pulse (alpha 0.75↔1.0, scale 1.0↔1.08, ~700 ms yoyo) with a matching glow,
  always on; no reduce-motion setting in this item.

- **Q4 — Where is the marker tuned?** Research: no repository or work-item answer
  needed — the repo has no motion/flash setting in `configStore`
  (`src/core/configTypes.ts`), and overlay styling constants live at the top of
  `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (`CHOICE_NEW_COLOR`, `CHOICE_ROW_PITCH`,
  …). Resolution: all new marker constants are module-level named constants in
  the same block, matching the existing convention (mirrors
  AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC3 "single source of truth"). Source: repo inspection
  of `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` and `src/core/configTypes.ts`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** – Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYTM7C00071Y1** – Change the current mineral count to a bar that fills (completed)
- **AH-0MVDV560Z002PSLT** – Full project test suite passes with the new changes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 00ffff, 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0muu1goau007rfvr, 0muv5clvo002zhs9, 0mv2n2591007ugpd (+397 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muv5clvo002zhs9, 0mv2n2591007ugpd, 0mvcfb00y004aq2z, absent, ac1 (+387 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+344 more)

## Problem

`implement.py parent` decides whether a child worktree contains work via `_git_path_has_changes()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`), whose docstring says it returns True when the worktree HEAD *differs* from the parent branch. A child worktree that is merely **behind** `dev` (HEAD != `dev`, but zero commits ahead and no dirty files) is therefore classified as "has changes" and `phase_parent` immediately runs `finish` on it.

Observed 2026-10-19 during the AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV epic:

1. `implement.py drive` started child AH-0MVF6XLBQ002GYWQ and its session was killed at the 3600 s timeout with a clean worktree (no edits, no commits).
2. While the drive was running, three unrelated commits landed on `dev`, so the child worktree was 3 commits behind.
3. `implement.py parent` reported `Child AH-0MVF6XLBQ002GYWQ has changes — running finish subprocess...` and ran `finish` on empty work. `finish`'s changed-scope selection was unavailable and fell back to a full-suite run (~10 min under load), which failed and reported `Failed to finish child`.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree with no dirty files and **no commits ahead of** the parent branch must be treated as "no work" (return the child as `next_child` for implementation), regardless of how far behind it is. The worktree placement guard should likewise not be affected.

## Suggested fix

- In `_git_path_has_changes()`, replace the "HEAD differs from parent branch" test with an ahead-count test (`git rev-list --count <parent>..HEAD` > 0) so behind-only worktrees are clean.
- Add a regression test covering: clean worktree at the fork base, clean worktree behind `dev`, dirty worktree, worktree with one commit ahead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A child worktree with no uncommitted changes and no commits ahead of the parent branch is not treated as having changes by `phase_parent` (covered by a unit test).
- **AC2:** A child worktree that is behind `dev` but has no local commits does not trigger a `finish` subprocess.
- **AC3:** Worktrees with commits ahead, or with dirty files, are still detected as having changes (no regression).
- **AC4:** The documented placement-guard contract (`docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` §"The placement guard") is preserved: a non-terminal child whose worktree is clean at the parent HEAD while the main checkout holds uncommitted changes outside `.worklog/` still fails closed, and a worktree that holds the work never triggers the guard (covered by a unit test).

## Scope and repository location

**The defect is not in this repository.** `implement.py` lives in the
**SorraAgents** repository (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`); the global
skill at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` is a symlink to
`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement`. AI_Hell contains no
`implement.py`, so this item is the **discovery report** and the fix (code +
regression tests + docs) is tracked in the SorraAgents counterpart
**SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5** (tag `discovered-from:AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81`).

This mirrors the established precedent **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB** →
**SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1**; as there, this item is closed when the SorraAgents fix
ships, not when the counterpart is created.

## Implementation plan (executed in SorraAgents)

1. **Tests first** — add `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py` built
   on throwaway git repositories/worktrees: clean at the fork base, clean and
   behind the parent branch, dirty file, one commit ahead; a `phase_parent` test
   asserting no `finish` subprocess for a behind-only child; and the
   placement-guard cases (clean behind-only child + dirty main checkout fails
   closed; worktree holding the work never triggers the guard). Confirm they fail
   against the current helper before changing it.
2. `_git_path_has_changes()` — keep the dirty-file check; replace the
   `HEAD != parent_branch` comparison with an ahead-count test
   (`git rev-list --count <parent_branch>..HEAD` > 0). Keep failing open when the
   count cannot be computed (missing ref, git error).
3. Update the docstrings of `_git_path_has_changes()` and
   `_has_worktree_changes()` to "dirty **or commits ahead of** the parent branch".
4. Re-check the two guard call sites that consume the helper —
   `_worktree_placement_violation()` (`phase_finish`) and
   `_child_main_checkout_violation()` (`phase_parent`/`phase_drive`) — against the
   documented guard contract (AC4); the step-1 tests pin the behaviour.
5. Update `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` if any wording still implies the
   "HEAD differs" rule.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_path_has_changes()`, `_has_worktree_changes()`, `_worktree_placement_violation()`, `_child_main_checkout_violation()`, `phase_parent()`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py` — new regression tests
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_extension.py` — existing patches of the helper (verify still valid)
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — placement-guard documentation

## Risks and assumptions

- The ahead-count semantics also change the placement guards' view of a
  behind-only clean worktree: with unrelated main-checkout dirt present, such a
  child now fails closed as "work done outside the worktree" instead of being
  silently re-run. This matches the documented guard contract (AC4), but should
  be called out in the commit message; if it proves disruptive for long-running
  drives, file a follow-up rather than diverging from the docs.
- Assumes the parent-branch ref is resolvable from inside the worktree (it is —
  linked worktrees share the main checkout's refs).
- No producer questions were needed: the defect, expected behaviour and fix were
  already fully specified in the intake description, so the plan pre-check
  (`plan-if-needed`) returned `skip` (Extra Small / Low) and planning reduced to
  the six automated review stages plus the cross-repo handoff above.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 (plan, Map): reviewed the intake description against
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` in SorraAgents; added AC4 (placement-guard
  contract), the scope/repository-location section, the implementation plan,
  `**Key Files:**` and the risks/assumptions section; created the SorraAgents
  counterpart SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5; stage → `plan_complete`.

# Intake Brief: Promo video scenarios (10+)

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map
**Status:** CONFIRMED — producer answered Q1 (b), Q2 (c), Q3 (a) on AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA.

## Problem statement

The game can record bot-flown gameplay clips (`npm run capture`) and compile
them into a promo, showreel and highlights (`compile-promo`), and the footage
can only show what the current run happens to contain. Today the only dev
scenarios are capture shortcuts (`boss`, `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) that jump
to an already-terminal boss fight; there is no curated set of scenes that
showcases the game's range. A promo video therefore needs dedicated,
reproducible scenarios — each pairing an interesting ship configuration with a
deliberate enemy wave — that the Watch Demo and the capture tooling can drive
on demand.

## Users

- **Producer / marketing** — wants a selection of visually distinct, reliably
  capturable moments to assemble into a promo video without hand-playing runs.
- **Player of Watch Demo** — sees varied, interesting bot-flown gameplay in the
  attract loop rather than the same default run each time.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, I want to record a boss battle, a pick-up frenzy and a dense
  enemy horde from fixed, reproducible scenarios so the promo covers each
  editorial category.
- As a player, I want the Watch Demo to fly a variety of bot/loadout and enemy
  combinations so the attract loop shows off the game's range.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (ten scenarios):** At least 10 scenarios are registered in the shared
  registry (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) and resolvable via the existing
  `scenario` URL query parameter, dev-gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV`
  exactly like today's scenarios — a production build and a normal run are
  unchanged.
- **AC2 (composition):** Every scenario starts from (i) the **single shipped
  ship config** paired with a **curated bot-tuning preset** in `src/data/
  bot-tuning.json` (optionally a starting weapon/loadout where existing
  mechanics support it) and (ii) a **hand-authored promo wave definition**
  composed from the existing spawner/movement machinery; each scenario is
  deterministic for a given seed and **bot-pilotable end to end**, sustaining
  enough watchable footage for a promo cut (target ≥45 s of action before the
  demo game-over dwell).
- **AC3 (range):** The scenario set evidences every promo editorial category
  from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` (`weapons`, `pickups`, `enemies`, `boss`) with at
  least one scenario each, and the set is ordered to open with a high
  action-intensity hook so the first captured cut has no dead air.
- **AC4 (capture integration):** `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` lists
  every scenario with its one-line effect, and `npm run capture --
  --all-scenarios` records one clean clip per scenario.
- **AC5 (tests):** Hermetic tests pin registry ↔ resolver parity, each
  scenario's bot-tuning preset and wave definition, and dev-only gating; an
  integration/demo check confirms a scenario is flown by the Watch Demo bot.
- **AC6 (docs):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, capture `--help` and
  `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.
- **AC7 (suite):** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scenarios are **dev-only**: gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV` exactly like
  today's scenarios (`src/core/devScenario.ts`); the shipped bundle stays
  inert.
- Single source of truth remains `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`; the game
  resolver and the capture CLI must not drift (registry ↔ resolver parity
  test enforced).
- Scenarios are **bot-flown** (the Watch Demo bot / competent bot), reproducible
  per seed, and must not require a human pilot to produce good footage.
- **Wave definitions are new hand-authored content**, but must be composed from
  the **existing spawner/movement machinery** (V/diver swarm, centipede, ghost,
  harvester, horde, strike, lane traffic, asteroid, boss/minion classes) — no
  new gameplay behaviour, so the gym↔game parity and duplicate-body guards in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` are not triggered.
- The shipped ship config (`ship-config.csv`) is **unchanged**; variety comes
  from bot-tuning presets and loadouts, not new ship rows.

## Existing state

- Ship configs: **one** row in `src/data/ship-config.csv` (asteroids scheme,
  thrust 300 px/s², maxSpeed 175 px/s). ShipConfig shape: `configTypes.ts:372`.
- Bot tuning: named presets via `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`, persisted in
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (currently one `Default` preset with `competent`
  + `human` layers); Watch Demo flies the current preset
  (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL).
- Waves: static `LEVELS` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), data-driven difficulty
  curves (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) sequenced by
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`; spawners per movement class in `src/waves/`.
- Power-ups/weapons: 16 power-up ids and 12 weapon drop ids
  (`src/powerups/types.ts`).
- Scenario infra: registry `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (3 entries),
  resolver `src/core/devScenario.ts`, capture CLI `--scenario /
  --list-scenarios / --all-scenarios`, page-side handle
  `window.__aiHellScenario` to release frozen runs.

## Desired change

Extend the dev-scenario registry so each entry carries the **bot-tuning preset
name** (and optional start loadout) plus its **hand-authored wave definition**
and optional seed. A new promo-wave module (`src/waves/promoScenarios.*`
naming TBD at implementation) hosts the hand-authored definitions, each built
from the existing spawner classes; the scenario resolver applies them at run
start through the existing seams (ship config loading, bot-tuning application,
wave sequencing, run seeding) rather than adding new gameplay. The result is a
catalogue of ≥10 named, documented promo scenarios driveable by
`npm run capture -- --scenario <name>` and the Watch Demo, covering all four
editorial categories and ordered to open with a high-intensity hook.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` — extend registry entries with bot-tuning
  preset + wave definition + optional loadout/seed metadata.
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts` — types for the richer entries.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — resolve and apply the preset and wave at run
  start; extend the resolved-scenario union.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` / `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — curated presets
  per scenario (Q1 answer: single ship, varied presets).
- `src/waves/` — new hand-authored promo wave definitions reusing existing
  spawner/movement classes, with tests (Q2 answer).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — scenario application seam at run start.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `--help`, README — documentation (AC6).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** scenarios are surfaced via the existing registry/URL-param
  pattern plus the capture CLI — no new menu picker unless requested (scope
  creep risk if a visible picker is added later; record as a separate item).
- **Assumption (Q1):** "interesting ship configuration" is delivered through
  bot-tuning/loadout variety on the single shipped ship — no new ShipConfig
  rows. Loadout variety limited to what existing mechanics support.
- **Assumption (Q2):** hand-authored waves live in a new dev-gated module
  composed from existing spawners — content, not new behaviour.
- **Risk:** hand-authored waves must be calibrated so the competent bot

# Intake Brief — Waves need more variation in enemy types

**Headline:** Make all 100 campaign waves draw from a wider enemy-type mix so no two sequential waves share the same enemy composition, while preserving each level's dominant-archetype identity and the existing difficulty ramp, fire boundary and determinism contract.

## Seed description

> Waves within a level should show more variation in enemy types.

## Problem statement

The shipped 10 × 10 campaign (100 waves) reads as repetitive within each level: Level 1 is Scout-only across all ten waves, Level 5 is Phaser-only, and the `fixed` filler waves in Levels 1–3 and the `fixed` showcases throughout are hand-authored compositions reused verbatim. Only L1W1, L1W2, L2W1 and L2W2 are `dynamic`. Within-level enemy-type variety is therefore the exception rather than the rule, and a player experiences long runs of the same enemies (e.g. ten Scout waves in a row at the start of the run).

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, I want each wave in a level to field different enemy types from the preceding wave, so the campaign feels varied rather than monotonous across a run.
- **As a player**, I want each level to keep a recognisable identity (its dominant archetype), so the onboarding ramp and the "Predictable Death" pattern-testing level stay legible.
- **As a designer**, I want the variation enforced as a campaign-wide invariant (not per-level hand-tuning), so future wave edits cannot silently reintroduce sequential repetition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No sequential repetition.** No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition. *Verification:* unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config; applies to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.
- **AC2 — Whole-campaign coverage.** All 100 waves are in scope (not just the opening four); every level's wave list shows more than one enemy archetype across its ten waves. *Verification:* per-level archetype-count assertion ≥ 2 across the ten waves.
- **AC3 — Level identity preserved.** Each level keeps its dominant archetype identity (Level 1 Scout-dominant, Level 5 Phaser-dominant; classic-arcade levels keep their showcase archetypes), varying *around* it with secondary archetypes. *Verification:* per-level dominant-archetype assertions; GDD §3.2 identity text still holds.
- **AC4 — Balance rules respected.** Generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves continue to satisfy the classification balance rules R1–R3 (opening formation-only, no all-chaser wave, bounded ranged mix). *Verification:* existing `waveBalance` audit/validator tests still pass over the rebuilt campaign.
- **AC5 — No regression of difficulty ramp and boundaries.** The non-decreasing target difficulty, the Levels 1–3 no-fire / Levels 4–10 fire boundary, and the wave-10 mini-boss encounters are unchanged; the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins pass. *Verification:* existing campaign regression and invariant suites.
- **AC6 — Determinism and reproducibility.** Same seed reproduces the same campaign; `curve`/`fixed` waves stay seed-independent, `dynamic` waves remain a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed). *Verification:* seeded-build equality tests as in the opening-variety item (AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B).
- **AC7 — Testing/validation.** New or updated unit/integration tests cover sequential distinctness, per-level identity, determinism and regression; **the full project test suite passes with the new changes**.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated, including code comments, `README.md`, the GDD (§3.2 level descriptions and the default-campaign note), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and any relevant docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- **Existing archetypes only** (consistent with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B): re-mix the 18-archetype roster (`scout`, `diver`, `tank`, `phaser`, `swarm`, `boss`, `asteroid`, `harvester`, `march`, `capturer`, `ghost-chase`, `ghost-ambush`, `ghost-flank`, `ghost-wander`, `grunt`, `raider`, `lane-traffic`, `orbital-strike`); do not invent new archetypes unless the producer explicitly requests them.
- **"Same enemies"** is interpreted as the same set of enemy archetypes in a wave's composition (order/spacing/count variations alone are not "different enemies"). The sequential-distinctness rule applies to generated waves as well (producer Q3 = c').
- **Level identity (Q2 = a):** the dominant archetype of each level is preserved; variety is added around it.
- **Mixed mechanism (Q3 = c'):** hand-authored `fixed` waves stay where a specific showcase/pin is required (wave-10 mini-bosses, classic-arcade debuts, L1 onboarding pin); `curve` waves stay deterministic; filler waves that are currently `fixed` may move to `dynamic` where safe, seeded per-run under R1–R3 guardrails.
- **Determinism contract** (AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT): `curve`/`fixed` seed-independent; `dynamic` pure function of (curve, pool, seed).
- **Fire boundary** (GDD §2.4/§2.5): Levels 1–3 do not fire; Levels 4–10 do. Generated waves derive fire rules from level number.
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): wave data/logic live in the shared core consumed by both `PlayScene` and the gyms; any divergence must be justified and recorded.
- **No target-curve re-tuning unless required** to satisfy AC1–AC3; if the ramp must move to break sequential repetition, it stays within the no-degeneracy + non-decreasing + strictly-rising aggregated difficulty constraints.
- **UK English** in all code comments, tests and documentation.

## Existing state

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — 100 rows; L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2 `dynamic`; most other L1–L3 rows `fixed`; L5W2 `dynamic`; Level 4+ mixed `curve`/`fixed`; wave 10 of every level `fixed` mini-boss.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS` hand-authored waves (used for `fixed`); Level 1 all Scout V-formations; Level 5 Phaser-only; classic-arcade showcases on Levels 6–10.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_FIXED_LEVELS`, `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES`, `defaultDifficultyCurves()`; per-wave mode overrides supported (`DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES[level]?.[wave]`).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — per-wave `generation` dispatch (`curve`/`fixed`/`dynamic`); `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION` for openings; seeded dynamic jitter.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — runtime auto-sequencer; `defaultCandidatePool()`; composition from `enemyDifficulty` targets.
- `src/core/waveBalance.ts` — pure R1–R3 rules + validator (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP); generator hard-constraints.
- Tests: `waveBalance.test.ts`, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`, `campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `sequencedLevels.test.ts` (incl. "Retuned default campaign (AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K)" and phaser-only filler pins), `WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 (L1 Scout V-formations).

## Desired change

- Extend enemy-type variety across all 100 waves so sequential waves differ in composition, per level identity (Q2 = a) and via the mixed fixed/curve/dynamic mechanism (Q3 = c').
- Introduce a campaign-wide sequential-distinctness invariant (producer Q1 = a + explicit rule), enforced in the shared builder/sequencer and tested.
- Keep hand-authored `fixed` waves where showcase/pin/identity requires; relax only what is needed to satisfy AC1–AC2.
- Where safe, convert currently-`fixed` filler waves to `dynamic` (seeded per-run variety) under the balance-rule guardrails; otherwise extend the authored `LEVELS` data to mix secondary archetypes into identity waves.
- Update documentation (GDD §3.2 level wording, default-campaign note, enemy-design docs, README, code comments).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — per-wave `generation` mode changes; possible minor target retunes for AC1–AC2.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — add secondary archetypes to identity-preserving `fixed` waves; keep showcases/mini-bosses.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — sequential-distinctness enforcement seam; possibly broaden `OPENING_WAVE_CURATION`-style curation to filler waves.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — composition constraint for sequential distinctness if enforced in the sequencer; pool/jitter tuning.
- `src/core/waveBalance.ts` — reuse R1–R3 validator for sequential-distinctness auditing (additive rule/named constant if needed).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES` updates if filler waves move to `dynamic`.
- Tests — `sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `campaignInvariants.test.ts` (or new `campaignVariety.test.ts`), `WaveManager.test.ts`, `configStore.test.ts`, `csv-seed.test.ts`.
- Docs — `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.2 + default-campaign note, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B** — Create more variety in the first 3-4 waves (completed v0.1.9): made L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic`; the partial-overlap precedent this item extends to all 100 waves.
- **AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP** — Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling (completed v0.1.13): R1–R3 rules + validator; must keep passing (AC4).
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** — Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign (completed): the ramp/regression pins AC5 preserves.
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration (completed): the mode dispatch + determinism contract.
- **AH-0MVCYANT6003SG5C / AH-0MVCRAR89009C8GZ** — 10-wave campaign data foundation + re-land (completed v0.1.14): the 100-wave grid this item varies.
- **AH-0MV398ZWL009TTOB** — Write campaign-level invariant tests (completed): precedent for campaign-wide invariants.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — identity vs sequential-distinctness tension (high).** Level 1 (Scout) and Level 5 (Phaser) must keep a dominant archetype yet not repeat across ten waves. *Mitigation:* allow 2–3 archetypes per level with the dominant sharing the most waves; assert "≥ 2 archetypes per level" plus "no adjacent identical composition", not "all ten waves distinct types".
- **Risk — ramp/regression disturbance (medium).** Re-mixing archetypes can shift `targetDifficulty` fit. *Mitigation:* reuse the retuned targets; retune only within the no-degeneracy/non-decreasing/strictly-rising constraints if required; keep the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins green.
- **Risk — sequencer target misses under a distinctness constraint (medium).** Enforcing "different archetype set from the previous wave" in `curve`/`dynamic` generation can push some waves off their `targetDifficulty` or shrink the candidate space. *Mitigation:* bias the sequencer towards the previous wave's complement (rules may trade exact target match for distinctness, following the R1–R3 precedence in AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP), or hand-author that wave as `fixed`; record resulting target error in the balance audit.
- **Risk — scope creep.** New archetypes, per-wave special mechanics, or reworking mini-bosses are out of scope; record as linked work items.
- **Assumption — existing archetypes only** (consistent with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B); no new archetypes unless the producer requests them.
- **Assumption — "same enemies" = same archetype set** in a wave's composition; count/order/spacing changes do not count as distinct.
- **Assumption — Q3 = c'** reads as the recommended mixed mechanism (authored `fixed` where pinned; `dynamic` for filler where safe), with the sequential-distinctness rule binding on generated waves too. If the producer intended otherwise, the mechanism sections of this brief change but AC1–AC3, AC5–AC8 stand.
- **Assumption — the sequential-distinctness rule is cross-wave, not cross-level** ("sequential within a level"); a wave-10 mini-boss and the next level's wave 1 are different levels and are not compared.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope — which waves need more enemy-type variation?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ88SK007XAFJ): **(a)** all 100 campaign waves, **plus the explicit rule: no two sequential waves should have the same enemies**. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q2: "Level identities — should the deliberate single-type levels stay pure?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ8CBE00748J3): **(a)** preserve each level's dominant archetype/identity but add variety around it. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q3: "Mechanism — deterministic authored waves or seeded dynamic per-run variation?" — Answer (producer, AH-C0MVNZ8FVZ005AERQ): **(c')** mixed, as in the recommended (c); the sequential-distinctness constraint applies to generated waves too. Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Research (agent): current campaign state audited (10 × 10 grid, mode ledger per wave); Level 1 Scout-only and Level 5 Phaser-only identities pinned by GDD §3.2/§2.5 and by `WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 / `sequencedLevels.test.ts` phaser-only pins; duplicate check performed (partial overlap only with AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B). Source: repo inspection + worklog search, this session (comments AH-C0MVNZ7UJ1005DJ9V).

## Related work (automated report)

_Appended after the find-related skill run (step 7)._

## Plan: feature decomposition

Decomposed into nine child work items following a **test-first, three-phase vertical-slice** cadence. Each phase cuts through data, code, tests and comments; the next phase's item descriptions are reviewed after each phase lands.

### Phase A — measure, then pilot the hardest case

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Campaign variety audit + failing invariants (AH-0MVSE6D2L0034SKG) | feature | Shared pure module `waveComposition` / `auditCampaignVariety` / `LEVEL_IDENTITY` + staged campaign assertions and the red-baseline audit snapshot |
| A2 | Relax single-type pins to identity-preserving (AH-0MVSE6F0O00689TT) | task | Convert "scouts only" / "phasers only" pins into dominance assertions (Q2=a) |
| A3 | Level 1 + Level 5 pilot: identity-preserving variety (AH-0MVSE6VIW009QG2E) | feature | Tracer bullet on the two highest-risk identity levels |

### Phase B — enforce, then rework the campaign

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Enforce sequential distinctness for generated waves (AH-0MVSE6XIO007BXYM) | feature | Seeded-deterministic constraint on `curve`/`dynamic` waves, R1–R3 precedence preserved |
| B2 | Authored variety rework — Levels 2–4 (onboarding) (AH-0MVSE7F090010EG3) | feature | Re-mix the no-fire onboarding `fixed` waves |
| B3 | Authored variety rework — Levels 6–10 (classic-arcade + finale) (AH-0MVSEFST20086D87) | feature | Re-mix the showcase/finale `fixed` waves; activates the campaign-wide AC1/AC2 aggregate |
| B4 | Document and verify the fixed/curve/dynamic mode mix (AH-0MVSE7GWU0074H5I) | task | Explicit mode ledger + drift test (Q3=c'); conversion only where authored data cannot express intent |

### Phase C — prove and document

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |

| C1 | Campaign variety regression, determinism and full-suite verification (AH-0MVSE7ILL000Y27B) | task | AC1–AC7 evidence, seed sweep, gym↔game parity, full suite |
| C2 | Documentation for campaign enemy-type variety (AH-0MVSE7KGQ002L2E2) | docs | GDD §3.2 + default-campaign note, enemy-design invariant section, README |

**Dependency order** (enforced with `wl dep`): A1 → A2 → A3 → B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → C1 → C2. A3 and B1 could run in parallel but are serialised because both touch the shared wave modules.

### Key design decisions recorded during planning

- **"Same enemies" = same archetype set**, counting wave groups **and** spawner opt-in flags (ghosts, centipede, horde, lane-traffic). Count/order/spacing changes alone do not satisfy AC1 — so re-tuning counts cannot fake variety.

- **Rules win over distinctness:** R1–R3 keep precedence, matching the existing precedence in AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP; a wave that cannot meet distinctness inside the acceptance band becomes authored `fixed` data instead of widening the band.

Each phase is a vertical slice, not a horizontal layer:

- **Phase A** delivers, in one green increment: the shared analysis code, its unit tests, the identity-pin contract, the authored Level 1/Level 5 data, the palette of comments and the audit report — proving the pattern end-to-end on the two hardest levels.

# Background scenes

> One-line headline: give each campaign level its own NASA space-photo background, swapped on level change with an unmistakable "warp" transition (hyperspace-style).

## Problem statement

The game currently renders all combat on a solid black backdrop (`GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR = '#000000'`), so the space setting is implied only by the neon vector art and every level feels visually identical. This work bundles a pool of NASA space photos and displays a distinct background per level, transitioning between them with an explicit "warp" effect so level changes are unmistakable and the campaign feels like travelling deeper through space.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, I want to see a different space background on each level and a warp transition between them, so moving to a new level feels like a jump through space and the run stays visually engaging."
- **Developer / capture pipeline:** "As a developer, I want deterministic background selection (same level → same background) so unit tests and recorded demo/capture video stay stable and repeatable."
- **Producer / reviewer:** "As the producer, I want the level-change transition to be unmistakable (the same standard already applied to phase-shift/wormhole effects, see AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU) without hurting gameplay readability."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At least 20 NASA space photos are bundled as game assets (public-domain / NASA-approved media) with attribution and licence notes; backgrounds render at the full 960×540 canvas (Phaser FIT scaling) and are a non-interactive layer that never occludes gameplay or intercepts input.
2. Each campaign level — the 10 levels in `LEVELS` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`) — gets a distinct background chosen **deterministically** from the pool via a level→background manifest; the background changes exactly on level change (the existing `levelCleared` → next-level path in `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent`), not per wave.
3. A "warp" transition effect plays while backgrounds change — timed to the existing `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s) transition pause — after which the new level's background is fully shown; the effect is deterministic, time-boxed, and does not block input or wave progression.
4. Gameplay readability is preserved: backgrounds are dimmed/desaturated beneath the neon vector art so enemies, bullets and the player ship stay legible (GDD §7.1 aesthetic, "2.5× keeps bullets legible against the neon background").
5. Background creation/swap logic lives in the shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/`) consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms (gym↔game parity convention in AGENTS.md); any gym divergence is documented.
6. Tests cover: deterministic level→background mapping, swap fires on level change (not wave), warp effect activates during the transition and completes within its duration, and the background layer does not intercept input; document updates (README, code comments, credits/attribution file with licences, GDD §3.2/§7.1 references as needed); the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Bundle, do not fetch at runtime.** Images are committed as repo assets (mirrors the existing `public/audio` precedent) — **confirmed by producer (2026-10-25)**. No runtime NASA API calls — avoids CORS, offline flakiness, and non-deterministic tests/demos.
- **Size/performance:** raw NASA photos are multi-megabyte; compress and resize to ≤ 1920×1080 (2× for HiDPI) JPG/WebP so the added bundle stays modest (target ≲ a few MB). Warp must use bounded, disposable effects (exported tuning constants + tracked/cleaned-up display objects, following the existing `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*` pattern).

# evaluate.mjs --tune: fail fast on unwritable --out and survive hard kill without dirty CSV

## Summary
During the 2026-10-21 end-to-end tune-loop verification (AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T), the negative-probe command

  node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out /proc/nope/x

hung for 166.6 minutes inside a single Pi bash call before being killed (exit 137 / SIGKILL) — the largest
single tool call of the day (2.8 h of ~11.8 h active agent time). Instead of failing fast on the unwritable
output path, the CLI runs both sweeps first and validates the output directory only at write time. A hard
kill also means the in-memory CSV restore in the finally block cannot run: the session log shows the CSV
dirty (M src/data/enemy-configs.csv, changed md5) immediately after the kill (clean now, restored by later
session activity). Root cause to confirm during implementation; hypotheses: (a) output-dir validation
happens only after the sweeps, (b) no internal watchdog/timeout on the sweep, (c) SIGKILL (OOM/timeout)
skips the finally-based restore, (d) the pipe to tail can mask the true exit.

## User stories
- As a developer running tune-loop verification I want --tune to validate --out (and the CSV path) up-front
  so an invalid path fails in seconds, not hours.
- As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe so even a hard kill never leaves the balance CSV
  edited in the worktree.

## Suggested approach
1. Validate options.outputDir and src/data/<tuneFile> before booting the SSR core or running any batch:
   a quick mkdir/writeability probe with a clear message and non-zero exit (ideally < 2 s).
2. Make edit/restore crash-safe: persist a small journal (target path + original bytes) beside the CSV
   before editing; restore/reconcile from the journal on next invocation (and document a manual repair
   path); do not rely solely on an in-memory finally.
3. Add a bounded-runtime watchdog or per-phase progress output for the sweep so an abnormal run cannot
   stall silently for hours; 2x200-tick games should take minutes, not hours.
4. Confirm the root cause with a repro before fixing (see hypotheses above); verify the observed exit code
   and CSV state in the repro.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The repro command above fails fast (< 2 s) with a clear "output directory not writable" diagnostic and
   a non-zero exit; demonstrated before and after the fix.
2. --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore and exits 0;
   existing behaviour is preserved and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.
3. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) at any point after the edit leaves the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run
   state, or a deterministic, documented repair path restores it exactly.
4. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes
   without hanging; the CLI help/docs mention the new validation.
5. Unit tests cover the writeability probe, the journal/restore under simulated kill, and the CLI exit
   codes; run under the project test policy (test skill).

## Context and references
- scripts/evaluate.mjs: main(), executeTune(), applyCsvEditFile(), restoreCsvFile()
- Related work items: AH-0MVBNITA0005VQGN (--tune CLI), AH-0MVBNISWE009QFBL (CSV edit guaranteed restore),
  AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (end-to-end tune-loop verification, where this was observed)
- Observed in session 2026-10-21T12-15-12-077Z (finding #2 of the session-time analysis)
- discovered-from: analysis session of 2026-10-21

# Intake brief — Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)

## Headline

Replace the mini-boss reward choice with a **spin-the-wheel** that always
delivers a guaranteed permanent upgrade: one bonus slot upgrades everything,
5 slots upgrade 3 picks, 10 upgrade 2, and the remaining 84 upgrade 1 — so a
mini-boss victory always makes the build meaningfully stronger.

## Problem statement

Mini-boss rewards currently offer a flat menu (upgrade any one owned item, or
unlock one locked weapon) which reads as a low-value chore rather than a
reward. The player wants a moment of anticipation that *always* pays out in
power, presented as a wheel of fortune spin over the power-ups the player has
invested in permanent slots.

## Users

- **Player (core loop):** after defeating a mini-boss, expects a celebration
  and a guaranteed, tangible power gain.
- **Demo/attract bot:** must not stall on the wheel; auto-spins after the same
  human-like delay as the hold-full choice (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F contract).

### Example user story

> As a player, when I defeat a mini-boss, I want to click a button to spin a
> wheel showing the power-ups in my permanent slots, watch it slow to a stop,
> and receive the landed upgrade(s) — so the reward feels like a gamble that
> always pays out, not a to-do list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Defeating a mini-boss opens a **wheel overlay** (the multi-option upgrade-or-unlock choice is gone): one wedge per **owned permanent kind** across the shared six-slot pool — power-up kinds **and** weapon drops — plus a single **bonus** wedge; play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice.
- Spinning is player-initiated (click/keyboard), the wheel animation starts fast and eases out (building tension; the outcome must not be predictable until it stops), and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly once.
- The spin outcome follows the **100-slot distribution**: 1 slot = bonus (every owned permanent kind +1 level), 5 slots = 3 upgrades, 10 slots = 2 upgrades, 84 slots = 1 upgrade. Multi-upgrade slots pick **distinct** owned kinds where possible and repeat a kind only when there are fewer owned kinds than the slot's count (a player with one owned power-up landing a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
- **Empty-owned fallback:** when the player owns no permanent kinds at a mini-boss defeat, the wheel is not shown and the existing hold-full-style three-option choice is offered instead, so a mini-boss always pays out.
- The run-scoped weapon-unlock feature and its reward options are **removed** from mini-boss rewards (locked-pool option builders, `getUnlockedWeapons` and the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field; `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bumped so stale checkpoints are rejected cleanly).
- Outcomes are drawn from the **run-seeded RNG** (no `Math.random()`), the distribution/resolver and the reward application live in shared modules the game and gyms both consume, and demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md`, checkpoint notes), including code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, including unit tests for the slot distribution/outcome resolver and PlayScene wheel-flow tests replacing the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): slot distribution and reward
  application must live once in shared modules consumed by `PlayScene` and any
  gym surface; no scene-private divergence.
- **Code-first visuals:** icons come from the existing code-drawn
  `src/powerups/icons.ts` (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets (GDD §7.2).
- **Seed reproducibility:** run-seeded RNG only; deterministic tests.
- **Launcher-agnostic overlay:** a single optional selection/result callback
  (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s `onSelect`), so any launcher can drive it.
- No ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation (test-slot policy); changed
  scope is run via the test skill.

## Existing state

- Defeating a mini-boss fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` → `openMiniBossReward`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`), which offers **one** upgrade-or-unlock choice:
  every owned permanent weapon/power-up level-up offer (built by
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`) plus every still-locked weapon from
  `MINI_BOSS_LOCKED_WEAPONS` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`). The overlay is the
  shared `MineralChoiceScene`; selection applies `applyMineralChoiceReward`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`, re-exported by
  `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`). Rewards are applied exactly once
  (`selectMiniBossReward` resets the open flag). See GDD §4.4.4
  (AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH).
- **Note (stale description):** the description's "choice of 5 random power
  ups" does not match current behaviour — the live reward is the
  upgrade-or-unlock menu described above; the wheel replaces *that*.
- Each wheel-relevant decision is a permanent kind in a **shared 6-slot pool**
  (`src/powerups/slots.ts`) covering both power-up kinds and weapon drops;
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) tracks permanent vs
  temporary levels and per-kind caps; the checkpoint
  (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) persists weapon/power-up levels and
  `unlockedWeapons` (the latter is removed by AC5).
- Demo mode already auto-selects the reward via `_randomDemoRewardIndex()`
  after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) — reuse this
  seam for auto-spin.

## Desired change

- New pure module (e.g. `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`): the 100-slot
  distribution (1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single), a weighted
  outcome resolver over owned permanent kinds, distinct-kind multi-upgrade
  selection (repeats only when fewer kinds than picks), cap-aware handling,
  injectable RNG.
- New launcher-agnostic overlay (e.g. `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`): one
  wedge per owned icon plus the bonus wedge, pointer, fast-starting/eased-out
  spin, landed-wedge highlight, click/keyboard to spin, result callback.
  Register in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward`: launch the
  wheel with the owned permanent kinds (from `resolveSlotState`/
  `getWeaponLevels`/`getPowerUpLevels`), apply the resolved outcome once
  through the shared reward machinery, fall back to the three-option choice
  when nothing is owned, and keep demo auto-spin.
- Remove the unlock feature (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts` locked-pool state and
  option builders, `PlayScene.getUnlockedWeapons`, the checkpoint
  `unlockedWeapons` field) and bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- Update GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` and checkpoint docs.
- Replace the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests in
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`; add deterministic unit tests for the
  distribution and outcome resolver.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — rework `openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward` to the wheel flow; fallback; demo auto-spin; drop unlock state.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (new) — pure 100-slot distribution + weighted outcome resolver, distinct-kind picks, caps.
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new) — launcher-agnostic wheel overlay: wedges, spin + ease-out animation, pointer, result callback.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — reuse `drawPowerUpIcon`/`drawWeaponIcon` for wheel wedges.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — owned permanent kinds feeding the wheel population.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — unlock machinery to be removed (AC5).
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` / `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — shared reward application for spin outcomes.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register the wheel scene.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — remove `unlockedWeapons`; bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — exercise the shared wheel/reward path (parity).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` (new) — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool (current behaviour being replaced).
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — AI bot reward-screen selection (demo auto-select contract to preserve).
- AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF — six-slot permanent loadout accounting (slot pool the wheel reads).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — power-up level store (permanent levels/caps applied by the wheel).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (shared modules requirement).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice overlay (pattern the wheel scene mirrors).

- AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD — Mini-boss/boss strength scales with player firepower (completed; adjacent balance context for reward power).
- AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y — Show current upgrades on the hull-full screen (open; same "player must see what they own" UI concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk:** celebration VFX/audio for the spin and rebalancing the
  1/5/10/84 split are follow-ups — record as separate work items, not scope.
- **Assumption (cap-aware draws):** when a drawn kind has hit its level cap,
  re-draw a non-capped owned kind; if every owned kind is capped the spin
  grants a fallback (minerals). Confirm during planning.
- **Assumption (mandatory spin):** the wheel always grants something and has
  no skip/decline path (a refusable "reward" recreates the perceived-nothing
  outcome).
- **Risk (unlock removal):** deleting the unlock feature removes a shipped
  progression mechanic; GDD §4.4.4 and the locked-pool docs must be rewritten
  in the same change so no doc promises unlocks. `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bump
  invalidates existing checkpoints (accepted: pre-release).
- **Risk (resolver/UI drift):** the wedge list and the weighted outcome must
  be derived from the same owned-kind snapshot; the scene must never compute

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

# Bot should be aware of screen wrap around (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG)

## Problem statement

The game's playfield is a wrap-around (torus) arena — the player ship, asteroids,
bullets and raider patrol all cross a screen edge and reappear on the opposite
side — but the AI bot's decision layer (`src/ai/`) is wrap-blind: it treats the
four bounding edges as solid walls it must not approach, never crosses a seam on
purpose, and measures every distance, bearing, aim solution, threat prediction
and nearest-selection along the raw (unwrapped) straight line. A human player
routinely uses the seam to chase, flee and angle shots; the bot cannot, so demo
play looks unhuman, the bot camps near the walls it wrongly fears, and it
systematically misjudges everything on the far side of an edge.

## Users

- **Players / viewers of the attract demo** — the demo bot is deliberately
  human-like (human reaction cadence, W/A/D controls, thrust feel); humans use
  the wrap, so a bot that refuses to is conspicuous.
- **Developers** — one coherent torus model in the decision layer, so future
  features (seam-aware enemy fire, new archetypes, tuning) share a single
  implementation instead of adding seam hacks.

### Example user stories

- As a **player watching the demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge to
  reach a target that is closer the other way, so its movement looks like a
  human's.
- As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
  shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite
  edge — so engagements play out in the whole wrap-around arena.
- As a **player**, I want the bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
  across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming.
- As a **developer**, I want one wrap-aware geometry implementation used by
  steering, aim, prediction and distance, so the model is consistent and
  testable, and the headless eval measures the same physics the bot faces in
  the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wrap-aware steering (movement)** — The four arena edges stop being walls in
   the steering safety/clearance test: both the legacy `evaluateVector`
   (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) and the competent `evaluateDirection`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) no longer reject a direction
   solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`, and steering toward an
   objective uses the **shortest wrapped path** (the closer of the raw bearing
   and the seam-crossing bearing to the objective's opposite-edge duplicate) so
   the bot crosses an edge to get to the other side — used deliberately when
   net-positive (Q2), never as a scripted trick. Unit tests cover each of the
   four edges: the wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter; an
   edge-crossing direction is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.

2. **Seam-aware aim & targeting** — Aim and target selection run on the torus:
   `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the
   shortest wrapped path, and `nearestTarget` / `nearestEnemyDistance` choose
   nearest by wrapped distance. When the wrapped route to an enemy, boss or
   mineral is shorter than the raw line, the bot points at the seam duplicate —
   firing off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge. Tests assert the aim
   angle equals the wrapped-path angle when that route is shorter, and that
   behaviour is unchanged when the raw line is already shortest.

3. **Seam-aware threat & hazard prediction** — `predictIncomingFire`
   (`worldModel.ts`), the competent `closestApproach` solves and the legacy
   path-crossing checks operate on the wrapped torus, so shots and moving
   hazards whose closest approach to the player crosses a seam are predicted and
   dodged. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's existing wrap-jump clamp is
   re-verified so it does not double-compensate once positions are modelled on
   the torus. Tests: a seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening (a
   raw-line-only view would miss it).

4. **`wallMargin` retired cleanly** — The now-meaningless wall-margin tunable is
   retired (or demonstrably re-purposed) across `botDecision.ts`,
   `competent/tunables.ts`, `style/fitting.ts` and `tuningFields.ts`; saved
   bot-tuning configs (`src/data/bot-tuning.json` and any gym-saved tunings)
   still load with the field gone (unknown-field tolerance), and the style-fit
   mapping is updated per the retirement. Documented in the tuning UI/docs.

5. **Eval parity** — The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is brought
   to wrap-parity with the game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of
   being culled off-field, and hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped
   path (matching the seam-aware aim the enemy wrap epic ships), so eval scores
   measure wrap-aware play. `arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet and
   seam-aim cases.

6. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit/integration tests cover wrapped steering
   (all four edges, raw vs. wrapped), seam aim, seam threat prediction, wrapped
   nearest-selection when raw and wrapped ordering differ, wall-margin
   retirement and eval parity. The human-like governor's reaction cadence,
   controls and thrust feel are unchanged (existing steering/bot integration
   tests stay green, plus new wrap scenarios). `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` are updated to describe the wrap-aware model. The full
   project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- One shared implementation in the bot decision layer — no divergent per-behaviour
  seam copies; share/adapt the seam maths the enemy wrap epic develops rather
  than reinventing.
- The human-like governor (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) is preserved: reaction
  cadence, W/A/D + optional reverse, seeded aim-skill noise and human-feel
  thrust presses are unchanged; wrap-awareness is a model property, not a
  scripted manœuvre.
- Use the seam when it is net-positive (Q2) — nearest-wrapped-path selection
  already yields that; no deliberate "wrap tricks".
- Do not change game physics (player/enemy/bullet wrap models); the bot's model
  must match the game, not alter it.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state (evidence)

- **Player wraps at all four edges** — `src/utils/movementModel.ts`
  (`if (x < 0) x += width; if (x >= width) x -= width;` and same for y). The
  headless eval arena drives the bot through the same `asteroidModel.tick(width,
  height)`, so the bot's own ship already wraps there.
- **Bullets wrap (game)** — `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` four-edge wrap;
  raider patrol wraps (`src/scenes/core/raiderPatrol.ts`). **Eval culls bullets
  off-field instead** (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` `offField`), and hostile fire
  there aims at the raw player position.
- **Bot treats edges as walls** — legacy `botDecision.ts` `evaluateVector`
  ("a direction is unsafe when it reaches a wall within `wallMargin`") and
  competent `steering.ts` `evaluateDirection` (same); both tuned by a
  `wallMargin` knob (`botDecision.ts:189`, `competent/tunables.ts:239`,
  `style/fitting.ts`, `tuningFields.ts:94`).
- **All geometry is raw Euclidean** — `competent/goals.ts` `nearestTarget`
  (`Math.hypot`), `competent/steering.ts` `bearingTo` / `interceptPoint` /
  `closestApproach`, `worldModel.ts` `nearestEnemyDistance` /
  `predictIncomingFire`, `botDecision.ts` distance / closestApproach.
- **Existing wrap compensation, not awareness** — `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`
  deliberately clamps spurious position jumps caused by wrap/respawn.
- **Tests assert the bot never wraps** — `botSteering.integration.test.ts`
  ("it never wraps the screen").
- **Enemy wrap epic in flight** — AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 makes enemies wrap and fire
  across seams (blocked child slices AH-0MVKXBV0O005Q77P, AH-0MVKXBWDY008R0YH,
  AH-0MVKXBSAD003VRMF, AH-0MVKXBTNJ003F1TC, AH-0MVKXBXQX003S7K5,
  AH-0MVKXBZ5N007LKH4); once it lands, a wrap-blind bot fails to aim or dodge
  seam fire at all.

## Desired change

Give the bot's decision layer a single, shared wrap-aware (torus) model:

1. **Wrap-aware steering primitives** in the decision layer — a wrapped bearing /
   delta helper alongside the existing raw geometry, with a small hysteresis at
   nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths so targeting does not flip duplicates every
   tick; use it for the four steering/clearance tests (legacy + competent) and
   for `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint`.
2. **Wrapped nearest-selection** — `nearestTarget`, `nearestEnemyDistance` and
   the collect/engage/evade distances use wrapped distance; evade flees across a
   seam when that is the safest separation.
3. **Seam-aware prediction** — `predictIncomingFire` and the closest-approach
   solves run on the torus; verify `hazardVelocity` still clamps only true
   teleports.
4. **`wallMargin` retirement** — remove/re-purpose the knob and its style-fit
   mapping; keep saved configs loading.
5. **Eval parity** — wrap enemy bullets, aim hostile fire along the shortest
   wrapped path, and update `arena.test.ts` so metrics capture wrap-aware play.
6. **Docs & tests** — update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` / `docs/EVALUATION.md`; add
   the wrap-scenario tests from AC1–AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — wrap-aware `evaluateDirection`
  (no wall-margin wall test), `bearingTo`, `interceptPoint`, `closestApproach`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `nearestTarget` and goal distances on
  the wrapped torus.

# Per-run progress output and opt-in sweep watchdog

## Goal (user story)
As a developer (or an agent) running a long tune sweep I want visible per-run progress and an
opt-in bounded-runtime guard, so an abnormal run can never stall silently for hours and so a
timeout aborts cleanly with the CSV already restored.

## Problem
`--tune` prints nothing between start and the final summary: `executeTune()` runs two
`runBalanceBatch()` sweeps with no output. When the 2026-10-21 negative probe stalled, the only
signal was a silent process for 166.6 minutes until an external SIGKILL (parent item
AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B). After slice 2 the known hang is gone, but a future stall in the sweep
itself (configuration-driven blow-up, non-determinism guard loop, I/O stall) would again be
invisible.

## Expected behaviour
- Every `--tune` run writes one progress line per completed game to **stderr**:
  `[tune] baseline 1/2 seed=1 policy=competent`, then `[tune] candidate 2/2 …`, then the phase
  transitions (edit applied, comparing, restoring). Stdout stays byte-identical to today so
  artifact/print parity and determinism are preserved.
- `--watchdog <seconds>` (default `0` = off) arms a bounded-runtime guard: on expiry the run
  prints a diagnostic naming the phase and the elapsed time, restores the CSV (journal from
  slice 3 + synchronous restore), and exits with a distinct code (124) rather than leaving a
  killed-but-dirty worktree.
- `--help` and `docs/BALANCING.md` document both.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Reuse the existing per-run hook instead of adding a second mechanism: `runBatch` already
   accepts `config.onRun` (`src/ai/eval/engine.ts`), but `runBalanceBatch()` in
   `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` does not expose it (and `CliOptions.telemetrySink` is ignored there).
   Add an optional second parameter `runBalanceBatch(options, hooks?: {onRun?})` that forwards
   `onRun`; keep the existing signature/behaviour when `hooks` is omitted.
2. In `executeTune()`, pass an `onRun` that writes the progress line to `io.err` (count games
   against `sweep.seeds.length * policies.length`) — no divergent copy of the sweep logic.
3. Add `--watchdog <seconds>` parsing to `parseEvaluateArgs` (validated: finite, >= 0;
   non-numeric → usage error exit 2), arm a timer in `executeTune()` and clear it in the
   existing `finally`; on expiry: diagnostic + `restoreCsvFile` + `process.exitCode = 124`
   (use `exitCode`, not `exit()`, so pending stderr drains and the pipe cannot mask the exit).
4. Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md` tune flags table + "Guards and guarantees"; assert in
   `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Risky assumptions
- A watchdog timer inside a synchronous sweep cannot interrupt a *blocking* synchronous call —
  it only fires between runs. Recorded as an accepted limitation: the guard catches stalls that
  yield to the event loop (the observed case is caught by slice 2's fail-fast path instead), and
  the progress lines remain the primary signal for a truly blocking stall. Document this
  limitation in `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- src/ai/eval/cli.ts
- src/ai/eval/engine.ts
- src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every --tune run emits per-run progress lines on stderr (never stdout), covered by a unit test that captures both streams.
2. An opt-in bounded-runtime watchdog (--watchdog <seconds>) aborts the sweep with a clear diagnostic naming the stalled phase, restores the CSV, and exits with a distinct non-zero code, covered by a test.
3. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes without hanging, with elapsed times recorded in a work-item comment.
4. Progress wiring reuses the shared runBatch onRun hook through runBalanceBatch (no divergent sweep copy in the shell), covered by cli.test.ts.
5. Artifact/print parity is preserved: stdout and the four tune artifacts are byte-identical to the pre-change output for the same seed/options (determinism tests stay green).
6. --help and docs/BALANCING.md document --watchdog, its default (off), its exit code, and the accepted limitation that a blocking synchronous stall cannot be interrupted, asserted by the docs guard.

Depends-on: slice 1 (repro + red tests)
